what: An email provider tightened sending limits the week a campaign launched
detail: A new outbound campaign was set to send a few hundred emails a day from a handful of inboxes. The week it launched, the provider lowered per-inbox limits and the plan had to be rebuilt across more inboxes with authentication set up by hand.
lesson: Infrastructure you depend on can change under you with no warning. Build the plan so one vendor's policy change does not sink it.
quote: "we rebuilt the whole sending plan in two days"

what: Doubled meetings booked for a pilot and still did not hit the number promised
detail: A three-month pilot started at four booked meetings a month and ended at eight. The proposal had promised ten, so the pilot was wrapped up rather than extended.
lesson: A result that beats the baseline can still be a broken promise. The number you sold is the number you are judged against.
quote: "eight is great, unless you said ten"

what: Priced a project on revenue share and could not verify the revenue
detail: An early project was priced as a percentage of new revenue. The customer's reporting was a monthly spreadsheet with no way to audit it. The next project was priced as a fixed fee.
lesson: Revenue share means your income depends on someone else's reporting. If you cannot audit it, you are not getting paid, you are hoping.
quote: "I was getting paid in trust, not dollars"

what: A weekend automation replaced a monthly software subscription
detail: Spent about two hours building a small script that sorts and drafts replies to routine inbound email. It replaced a $40/mo tool and does the one job better because it was tuned on real examples.
lesson: When building the narrow version takes an afternoon, paying monthly for the broad version gets harder to justify.
quote: "two hours of work, forty dollars a month back"

what: A recipe that only works in the test kitchen
detail: A workflow demo ran perfectly on clean sample data and broke on the first real export, which had merged cells and blank headers. The fix took longer than the demo.
lesson: A demo proves the idea. The messy input proves the product.

what: Learned to bake bread during a slow quarter
detail: A quiet stretch between projects turned into a few weekends of bread experiments. Most loaves were flat. The one that worked came from following the recipe exactly once before improvising. PERSONAL - use only if cleared for a given piece.
lesson: Not every story in the bank is for publication. This card exists to show how the PERSONAL flag works.
quote: "follow the recipe once, then break it"
